Definition: from G4235; gentleness, by implication, humility:--meekness.
BiblicalUsage: Praiotes is meekness, gentleness, and the King James reads this spelling in the great passages. It is the fruit of the Spirit in Galatians, and the lowliness and meekness Paul urges on the Ephesians. The other spelling carries the same virtue in the remaining verses, so the two spellings are one word in two dresses.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that meekness is the Spirit's fruit, not my own achievement, and it grows where the Spirit rules.
